artworks.title: Seduction Scene on a Terrace by Moonlight
artworks.medium: Opaque watercolor with gold on paper
artworks.curatorNote: A full moon hangs over a palace terrace. Notice the white canopy, the water pipe on the floor and the gold flecks scattered across the mount. The artist built the whole scene from opaque watercolor with gold on paper.
artworks.lesson: Mughal court painters worked in opaque watercolor, which sits on the paper as a solid layer instead of a see-through wash. That is why the moon and the pale terrace glow so brightly against the dark sky. Gold was added for shimmer.
artworks.alt: A full moon over a pale palace terrace at night. A figure reclines under a white canopy while attendants stand nearby. The scene is framed by a gold border on speckled paper.

puzzle.prompt: Which medium did the painter use for this moonlit terrace?
options: Opaque watercolor with gold on paper
puzzle.hint: The plaque says the paint sits as a solid layer, and the mount is flecked with a precious metal.
puzzle.nudge: Think about what makes the moon and terrace glow against the dark sky, and what glitters on the border.
puzzle.explanation: The plaque names opaque watercolor with gold on paper, which is why the moon and terrace shine.

artworks.credit: Mughal, Seduction Scene on a Terrace by Moonlight, 18th century. Everett and Ann McNear Collection. Art Institute of Chicago, CC0 public domain. https://www.artic.edu/artworks/120669

artworks.title: The Girl by the Window
artworks.curatorNote: A girl in her nightgown stands in a dark room and looks out at a brighter night. Her face is hidden. With one hand she draws back a pale curtain, the lightest shape in the room besides the window itself.
artworks.lesson: Edvard Munch painted this in 1893 with loose, open brushwork. Deep browns, blues and greens fill the room, while light blues and pink whites mark the girl and the window. The contrast pulls your eye to the one gesture in the picture.
artworks.alt: A brown-haired girl in a nightgown stands in a dark room, gazing out a window into a brighter night. Her face is unseen and her hand draws back a pale curtain.

puzzle.prompt: The girl looks out at the night. What does her hand draw back?
puzzle.hint: It hangs at the window and is one of the lightest shapes in the dark room.
puzzle.nudge: Look at her hand. It is moving something soft and pale that hangs beside the glass.
puzzle.explanation: Her hand draws back the pale curtain, the lightest shape in the dark room.

artworks.credit: Edvard Munch, The Girl by the Window, 1893. Searle Family Trust and Goldabelle McComb Finn endowments; Charles H. and Mary F. S. Worcester Collection. Art Institute of Chicago, CC0 public domain. https://www.artic.edu/artworks/154235

artworks.title: Pardon in Brittany
artworks.curatorNote: A rider on a pale horse rises above a sea of white caps at dusk. The whole sky is washed in rose-mauve, and tiny warm flecks of light glow among the crowd like candle flames.
artworks.lesson: Gaston La Touche painted this crowd in 1896 with soft, blended strokes in oil. The sky stays one gentle rose-mauve tone, so the small warm lights below read as the brightest points in the picture.
artworks.alt: At dusk a dark rider on a pale horse rises above a crowd of white-capped people. The sky is rose-mauve and small warm lights glow among the crowd.

puzzle.prompt: Which color washes the dusk sky above the crowd?
puzzle.hint: It is a soft blend of pink and purple, the color of a late sunset.
puzzle.nudge: Look above the rider. The sky is gentle and pale, not dark and not golden.
puzzle.explanation: The sky is washed in rose-mauve, which makes the small warm lights below stand out.

artworks.credit: Gaston La Touche, Pardon in Brittany, 1896. Mr. and Mrs. Martin A. Ryerson Collection. Art Institute of Chicago, CC0 public domain. https://www.artic.edu/artworks/111656

artworks.title: Self-Portrait
artworks.curatorNote: The painter turns toward us against a deep red-brown ground. He holds a brush in one hand and a palette in the other. His collar and face catch the light while the rest fades into shadow.
artworks.lesson: Walter Shirlaw painted himself in 1878. Showing the tools of the trade in a self-portrait declares the sitter to be a working artist. The dark ground makes the pale collar and face the focus.
artworks.alt: A mustached man in a brown coat turns toward the viewer against a deep red-brown background. He holds a brush in one hand and a palette in the other.

puzzle.prompt: Besides his brush, what does the painter hold to show his trade?
puzzle.hint: Painters rest it on one arm and mix their colors on it.
puzzle.nudge: Look at his other hand. It carries a flat, curved board covered in paint.
puzzle.explanation: He holds a palette, the board where painters mix color, which marks him as a working artist.

artworks.credit: Walter Shirlaw, Self-Portrait, 1878. Gift of Joseph M. Rogers. Art Institute of Chicago, CC0 public domain. https://www.artic.edu/artworks/11

artworks.title: Approaching Storm
artworks.curatorNote: Heavy gray clouds roll in over a sandy beach. Ladies in wide skirts, a child in red and a small white dog wait beside tall wooden huts on wheels. A pennant snaps from a pole at left.
artworks.lesson: Eugène Louis Boudin painted this in 1864 on a small oil panel. He was known for skies, and here the cloud-filled sky takes up most of the picture. The pale huts catch the last light before the weather turns.
artworks.alt: A beach under dark gray storm clouds. Well-dressed figures gather beside pale wooden bathing huts on wheels while a pennant flies from a tall pole.

puzzle.prompt: What do the beachgoers gather beside as the storm approaches?
puzzle.hint: Swimmers once changed inside these small pale buildings and rolled them toward the water.
puzzle.nudge: Look at the tall pale shapes with peaked roofs standing on the sand.
puzzle.explanation: The plaque points to the wooden bathing huts on wheels, the pale shapes that catch the last light.

artworks.credit: Eug├¿ne Louis Boudin, Approaching Storm, 1864. Mr. and Mrs. Lewis Larned Coburn Memorial Collection. Art Institute of Chicago, CC0 public domain. https://www.artic.edu/artworks/27764

artworks.title: Fishing Boats with Hucksters Bargaining for Fish
artworks.curatorNote: Boats ride rough waves under storm clouds, and the whole canvas is large and loosely painted. The title tells you what the people on the water are doing: bargaining over the catch.
artworks.lesson: Joseph Mallord William Turner, usually called J. M. W. Turner, painted this sea in 1837 to 1838. He cared more about weather, light and the motion of water than about crisp outlines. That is why the waves and clouds blur together.
artworks.alt: A large marine landscape of boats on rough waves beneath storm clouds.

puzzle.prompt: Which painter, known by the initials J. M. W., made this stormy sea? Give the surname.
puzzle.hint: He loved weather, light and moving water more than sharp outlines.
puzzle.nudge: The plaque spells out three names ending in a surname that also names a person who turns things.
puzzle.explanation: Joseph Mallord William Turner, known as J. M. W. Turner, painted this blurred, stormy sea.
